parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment consists of three questions: "How does this analysis extend to more general cases? Can it handle more general Markov chains? What if there is FFN and nonlinearity on top of the attention layer?" These are clarification questions that imply the authors should address these aspects in the paper. The action is not explicitly stated as a directive (e.g., "Add a discussion of..."), but it can be inferred that the authors need to extend the analysis to these scenarios. While the questions name the topics to consider (more general Markov chains, FFN and nonlinearity on top of attention), naming the topic is not the same as specifying how the action should be implemented; the rubric's concreteness criterion concerns how to carry out the change. The comment offers no guidance on how to extend the analysis, handle more general Markov chains, or incorporate FFN/nonlinearity — no methods, experiments, or revisions are suggested. 'Discussing or analyzing these cases' remains vague, so the authors know what is being asked about but not how to apply it to the draft. Under the rubric, this corresponds to an implicitly stated action that is vague and lacks detail on how to apply it.
